---
title: "`ev_volcano()` — Cartesian volcano plot"
---

## Purpose

Draw a standard volcano (log2 fold-change vs $-\log_{10}$ significance) for one
contrast, colouring points up / down / ns and labelling hits by a chosen rule.

## When to use

When you want a plain volcano without the enrichment ring — for QC, a
supplementary panel, or to compose into a multi-contrast figure with
`ev_compose()`.

## How it works

Subsets `data` to the named `contrast`, picks the y-axis column from `p_method`
(`pi_eq2`/`pi_eq1` → the π-score columns, `raw_p` → `P.Value`, `adj_p` →
`adj.P.Val`), and plots $-\log_{10}$ of it against `logFC`. A point is called
**up** or **down** when it passes both `p_threshold` and `logfc_threshold` in the
right direction, otherwise **ns**. Colours come from `theme$palette`. Labels are
chosen by `ev_select_labels()` according to `label_mode`:

- `"none"` — no labels (default)
- `"top_per_direction"` / `"top_total"` — top `label_n` by `label_rank_by`
- `"all_significant"` — every significant point
- `"explicit"` — only the symbols in `label_genes`

Labels are placed with `ggrepel` (seeded for reproducibility).

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `p_method` | `"pi_eq2"` | π-score y-axis matches the significance call used elsewhere |
| `p_threshold` | `0.05` | conventional significance cutoff |
| `logfc_threshold` | `log2(1.5)` | 1.5× fold-change, a common effect-size floor |
| `label_mode` | `"none"` | uncluttered by default; opt in to labels |
| `label_n` | `10` | cap for the top-* modes (per direction for `top_per_direction`) |
| `label_rank_by` | `"significance"` | rank labels by significance, not effect size |
| `label_genes` | `NULL` | symbols to label when `label_mode = "explicit"` |
| `theme` | `ev_theme()` | locked palette + theme |

## Literature

No method-specific citation; see [methods](../methods.qmd).

## Example

```r
ev_volcano(dep, contrast = "CTLvMITO",
           p_method = "adj_p", label_mode = "top_per_direction",
           label_n = 8)
```
